reason: E1 supports that configurational disorder in spinel oxides enhances CO oxidation and stability, but it concerns bulk spinel catalysts, not HEO overlayers on alloys. E2 supports that HEO supports stabilize Pt nanoparticles against sintering and hydrothermal deactivation, but it involves Pt nanoparticles on an HEO support, not an HEO overlayer on a multi-principal-element alloy. The premises about depositing a porous HEO overlayer, the specific Gibbs free energy mechanism, and oxygen vacancy-mediated poisoning resistance are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides improves CO oxidation activity and stability (E1).
High-entropy oxide (HEO) supports confer exceptional sinter-resistance and hydrothermal stability to Pt nanoparticles (E2).
A porous HEO overlayer can be deposited onto an alloy catalyst to create a sinter-resistant scaffold.
The HEO layer will suppress nanoparticle sintering and growth by lowering Gibbs free energy through multicomponent mixing.
The HEO layer will create oxygen vacancies that mitigate poisoning by H2O and NO.
